spec.idea: Flat 1-D indexing over rows*I with 8 elements per thread via two packed_half4 loads/stores (alignment-safe for odd I, overloads for device/constant inputs), fast::exp, scalar tail.

Single 128-bit load per input and one 128-bit store per thread (8 elems, 16B-aligned since base is a multiple of 8), with fast::exp2 and a folded log2e constant to shorten the per-element math, plus a scalar tail.

Single 128-bit load per input and one 128-bit store per thread, with exp2 (clamped to avoid overflow) and a fast reciprocal in place of a full divide, and a*b multiplied first to shorten the dependent chain after the transcendental.

16 elements per thread with four independent 128-bit loads issued before any math (more bytes in flight for the large shapes), using exp2 with a clamp, a fast reciprocal and a*b multiplied first, plus a scalar tail.

16 elements per thread with all four 128-bit loads issued before any math for more memory-level parallelism, smaller 128-thread groups, and exp2 with a true divide (no fast reciprocal); scalar tail for ragged sizes.
